newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma orders govt spending cut plan checked.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma orders govt spending cut plan checked.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament on Wednesday ordered the Audit Chamber to verify the government's 1997 spending cuts bill, likely to be the subject of heated debate.

The government has brought in a sequestration bill, cutting planned spending, under terms of the budget law, which requires mandatory spending cuts if revenues fall below 90 percent of planned levels in any one quarter.
Revenues in the first quarter were sharply below budgeted levels.
The government cuts would total 108 trillion roubles, with cuts on most items of 55 percent, and cuts in priority items of 30 percent. Some social programmes would not be cut.

The Duma ordered the Audit Chamber, which monitors government spending on behalf of parliament, to finish its review by May 20, when the Duma and Federation Council upper house are to hold joint hearings on the sequester plan.
The sequestration bill will be debated on May 21 after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin reports on the first quarter spending and revenues to the Duma.
Communist deputies have condemned the government's spending cut plans and called for money supply to be doubled to ease the financial crisis. The central bank has rejected the idea.
